I read the whole file. It has three theorems and no simp attributes, simp sets or local simp lemmas. I checked three things.

1. Mathlib's `Polynomial.resultant_map_map` is `@[simp]`, but only at explicit indices: `resultant (f.map φ) (g.map φ) m n = φ (resultant f g m n)`. At the default indices, `resultant (p.map φ) (q.map φ)` uses `(p.map φ).natDegree`, so Mathlib's lemma does not match. The file's `Monic.resultant_map_map` fills that gap. It has a `p.Monic` hypothesis that simp can only discharge when `hp` is a hypothesis, or via the `Monic.map`-style simp lemmas. I think leaving it unmarked is reasonable. The only uses are explicit rewrites, `rw [← hp.resultant_map_map φ]` in this file, and I found no `simp` call that needs it. Tagging it `@[simp]` would be a speculative recommendation.
2. I read the two downstream uses of `Monic.isCoprime_map_iff`, in Hensel.lean line 548 and Idempotents.lean line 253. Both apply it explicitly with `.mp`, so a simp lemma isn't needed.
3. `Monic.isCoprime_map_iff_eq_isCoprime_map` states an equality between two proofs of an `Iff`. That is a proof-irrelevance fact and not a simp-interface concern. I did not evaluate it under other rubrics.

I found no loop, competing rule, bad orientation or missing canonical simp lemma that the sources support. I did not run Lean.
